title: Enforce Independent Measurement and Prefer C++ Toolchain
summary: Enforces structural validation (measurement) and computational rigor (C++ preference).

independent_measurement_enforcement.rule: Independent measurement is REQUIRED for any claim at C4 or higher.

new_checks.name: independent_measurement_check
logic: if requested_level >= C4 AND independent_measurement_count < 1 → downgrade_to_C3
if requested_level >= C5 AND independent_measurement_count < 1 → downgrade_to_C4

new_checks.name: cpp_preference_check
logic: if cpp_tool_available_for_model_class == true AND selected_tool_language == 'python' → flag_warning
if strict_mode == true AND cpp_tool_available_for_model_class == true AND selected_tool_language == 'python' → downgrade_confidence

SIM_DESIGNER: For any intended claim level C4 or higher, MUST include at least one independent measurement tool.
When both C++ and Python tools exist for the same model class, MUST select C++ unless explicitly justified.
If Python is used when C++ is available, must log justification in run metadata.
Prefer C++ tools for all production, validation, and high-rigor runs.
EXECUTOR: Record implementation_language for each tool execution.
Record whether a C++ equivalent tool was available.
GOVERNANCE_CHECK: Verify independent measurement presence for any claim at C4 or higher.
Verify measurement evidence is linked and uses mechanism_class='measurement'.
Check if Python tools were used when C++ equivalents exist.
If violation detected, flag cpp_preference_violation = true.
If strict_mode is enabled, reduce claim confidence or block promotion.
Require explicit justification for any Python usage when C++ exists.

rules: C++ tools are REQUIRED for C4+ claims unless unavailable.
Python-only execution is allowed for exploratory or L0–L2 runs.
Python usage in C4+ must include justification and be flagged.

cpp_preference_violation.trigger: Python tool used when C++ equivalent exists

rollback_notes: Remove claim_gate checks and tool selection policy entries.
